why: For needles under 200 chars findClauseRange returns the head match and must NOT expand to a separately-found tail — expansion would absorb everything up to the next occurrence of that tail word/phrase, which is often unrelated text. The target here is 52 chars (well above tailCandidates' own 40-char floor, so tailCandidates genuinely produces real candidates rather than short-circuiting empty) and the document contains an earlier, unrelated paragraph that happens to quote the target's own tail phrase verbatim. Verified by mutation: against the real, unmodified word.ts this issues exactly 1 body.search query and returns the full target; against a scratch copy with only the <200 bail deleted, it issues a second query, latches onto the earlier decoy occurrence of the tail phrase, and expandTo produces a short, wrong span — proving the bail (not the tailCandidates length floor) is what keeps this case correct.
